Load libraries and load in data

```{python}
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from lets_plot import *
LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)

url = "https://byui-cse.github.io/cse110-course/lesson11/life-expectancy.csv"

df = pl.read_csv(url)
```



REVIEW EXERCISE:
Just look at the United States, rename the last column to "Life".
---

```{python}
usa = (
    df.filter(pl.col("Entity") == 'United States')
    .rename({'Life expectancy (years)': 'Life'})
)
```

# Plotting a basic histogram
```{python}
(
    ggplot(data=usa)
        +geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = 'Life'))
)
```

# Task 1 USA Life expectancy
```{python}
(
    ggplot(data = usa)
        +geom_line(mapping = aes(x = 'Year', y = 'Life'))
        +scale_x_continuous(limits = [1900, 2000])
)
```

# Task 2 
using markers (note: dont overlap the text with the line like this one does, its fine for example but not submission)
```{python}
(
    ggplot(data = usa)
        +geom_line(mapping = aes(x = 'Year', y = 'Life'))
        +scale_x_continuous(limits = [1900, 2000], format = 'd', breaks = list(range(1900,2000,10)))
        +geom_rect(xmin = 1915, xmax = 1920, ymin = 45, ymax = 60, fill = "red", alpha = .2)
        +labs(
            title="Life Expectancy in the United States Over Time",
            caption = ("Overall life expectancy has an upward trend as time goes on. Notable points include 1918-1920, where the spanish flu and WWI caused a significant decrease, marked in red. The last decrease was in 1943, which is marked by the blue dashed line.")
        )
        +theme(plot.caption.position = "plot")
        +geom_text(x = 1926, y = 45, label = "Spanish Flu and WWI", size = 5, color = "black", hjust = 0)
        +geom_segment(x = 1925, xend = 1920, y = 45, yend = 50, color = "red", arrow = arrow())
        +geom_vline(xintercept = 1943, color = "blue", linetype = 3)
        +geom_text(x = 1945, y = 65, label = "Last decrease in 1943", size = 5, color = "black", hjust = 0, angle = 270)

)
```
